NgraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale:
D37 completes a change the repository has already made once. C-APPROVAL-FINGERPRINT relocated the human's act from writing the status attribute to supplying the ratification while the tool performs the write. applied is the transition that did not get that treatment. The structural argument is unchanged: a status transition is where a bundle acquires or loses authority, so a hand-edited attribute is a hole by construction. More careful instructions cannot close it.
The verb is small, local, and shippable now. Attestations are a programme with their own board entry. They must not share a bundle. The record this verb writes is attributes on Decision, the same opening C-APPROVAL-FINGERPRINT used, so a later Signatures-like collection can land as further attributes without invalidating the event (a child still would).

Alternatives.Alternative: Make gate apply the writer. Rejected. D37 and A29.2 constrain the gate: evaluation must not mutate as a side effect. The usage text at command.ts:492 would become a lie. C-APPROVAL-FINGERPRINT revised gate purity for approve only and left apply, archive, and verdict as evaluate-and-record. A dedicated root is the explicit trigger invariant 8 asks for.

Ship ngrace lifecycle finish, the name D1 used. Rejected. F224's owner sentence names ngrace apply with argv token change. The supersede precedent is a verb named for the transition, not a lifecycle family. D1.1's dry-run nested apply flag on a command named apply is theatre; the invocation is the trigger.

Put fingerprint and artifact on a second gate apply Decision and leave GateId closed. Rejected. C-APPROVAL-FINGERPRINT bound refuse, apply, and archive Decisions to never carry those attributes. Mixing the evaluation permit with the write would make newest apply Decision mean two different events. Expanding the parse vocabulary (VALID_GATES and GATE_DECISION_GATES) with applied names the writer without adding a gate subcommand, which is the argument C-SUPERSEDE-COMMAND used against a superseded GateId: supersede had a lint-checked status plus Replacement and no F86 gap; this transition does. Evaluation GateId stays closed so evaluateGate("applied") does not type-check.

Widen GateId to include applied and make evaluateGate exhaustive, throwing on applied. Rejected. evaluateGate("applied") would compile. A runtime throw is an assertion the split type already prevents. That shape forces src/gates/core.ts; the split does not. Archive as implicit default is safe only while the parameter type cannot name applied.

Mint no Decision, like supersede. Rejected. F224 and D37 require a fingerprint of the applied bytes and a ledger record of the write. F86 is exactly a gate Decision standing in for work the gate did not do. A verb that writes and moves and still appends nothing reproduces that gap.

Re-evaluate apply and archive inside the verb. Rejected. That duplicates the gates and invites the purity hole D37 forbids. The verb reads hasPermittingDecision. Stale permits are the same risk today's hand-edit already has.

Ship D1.3 applied-without-record detection in this bundle. Rejected. Every existing applied archive is the pre-writer shape. Widening review to applied would report the corpus at once, the outcome C-APPROVAL-FINGERPRINT AC-ARCHIVE-SILENT forbade. The write Decision is what makes a later detector possible. Owner: P3.7.
Spawn git mv. Rejected. The supersede precedent renameSyncs and does not spawn git. Close commits stay the operator's. git mv was the hand form of the same filesystem rename.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Typed attestations on the gate-applied Decision records. D37 sequences them after the verb. Envelope, purpose-inside- the-signed-statement, and issuer-agnostic verification belong to RM-VERIFIED-APPROVAL.
D1.3 / P3.7 review finding for applied with no matching gate-applied record, with a non-retroactive trigger that does not flag the legacy corpus.

Scenarios.Scenario: Happy path. Bound pass recorded, gate apply permits, epoch folded, gate archive permits, ngrace apply writes both artifacts, fingerprints, appends two Decisions, renameSyncs into archive/. Operator commits.
Missing archive permit. Verb refuses naming archive, writes nothing. Operator runs gate archive, then retries.
Crash after status writes and Decision append, before rename. Bundle sits applied under active/. Re-running the same verb skips matching writes, skips matching fingerprints, and does the rename.
Force. Apply permit missing, operator supplies reason. Verb writes, fingerprints, moves, and records forced true. Dest already exists still refuses.
